name: Aave V3 wstETH CAPO oracle misconfiguration — wrongful liquidations (Mar 10, 2026)

window_utc.trough: 2026-03-10T11:47:00Z (approx — bad snapshotRatio executed on-chain one block after submission; max mispricing -2.85% applied from that block)
window_utc.end: 2026-03-10T23:59:00Z (acute phase; Chaos Labs cut wstETH borrow caps and realigned snapshot parameters the same day — exact correction minute not verified. Reimbursement tail ran into spring 2026)

speed: Near-instantaneous onset: the bad snapshotRatio executed on-chain one block after the 11:46 UTC submission, and permissionless liquidation bots cleared all 34 eligible positions within the following minutes to hours — no warning, no market signal, nothing a borrower could react to. Detection, borrow-cap cuts and parameter realignment happened the same day; full financial resolution (reimbursement) took roughly days-to-weeks via governance.
summary: Aave v3 CAPO, 10.03.2026, 11:46 UTC: некорректный snapshotRatio в CAPO-обвязке оракула (риск-провайдер Chaos Labs) капнул wstETH на −2.85% против живого курса БЕЗ движения рынка — permissionless-боты за минуты ликвидировали 34 здоровые позиции на ~$26-27M (штрафы ~499-512 ETH). Bad debt НОЛЬ, USDC-саплаеры не потеряли ни цента (протоколу даже плюс в резервы), DAO возместило заёмщикам. Класс риска: не манипуляция, а КОНФИГУРАЦИОННАЯ ошибка профессионального провайдера в автоматизированном пайплайне параметров — на крупнейшей площадке книги. Для саплаера — операционный риск площадки, не кредитный. Книга SPA на 2026-08: aave_v3 40% / pendle (PT_USDC) 20% / maple 15% / morpho_steakhouse 15% / кэш USDC 10%.

timeline.event: Follow-up '[Direct to AIP] Re-enable wstETH Borrow Caps on Ethereum Core and Prime (Post CAPO Incident)' (thread 24295) restores the borrow caps cut during the emergency response.

Chaos Labs detects and intervenes: temporarily reduces wstETH borrow caps and manually realigns snapshotRatio/snapshotTimestamp, restoring correct pricing. Founder Stani Kulechov confirms a CAPO misconfiguration in an external risk tool, not a protocol vulnerability; zero bad debt; core pools and depositors unaffected.

Chaos Labs' off-chain Edge Risk engine computes and submits a snapshotRatio update to the wstETH CAPO adapter on Aave V3 Ethereum; AgentHub (BGD Labs' automated execution layer) fires it on-chain one block later via Chainlink Automation.

Misconfiguration goes live: the update tried to move snapshotRatio from ~1.1572 toward ~1.2282 but a growth-rate constraint capped it at ~1.1919, while snapshotTimestamp jumped unimpeded to an anchor ~7 days in the past. CAPO's extrapolated ceiling comes out at ~1.1939 wstETH/ETH vs the live on-chain rate of ~1.2285 — Aave prices wstETH ~2.85% below true value with no market move (approx ts: one block after submission).

Liquidation cascade (intraday, exact minutes unverified): bots liquidate ~10,938 wstETH across 34 high-leverage ETH-correlated E-Mode accounts on Aave V3 Ethereum Core and Prime instances — ~$26-27M notional — capturing ~499-512 ETH in liquidation bonuses.

CoinDesk and other outlets report the 'rare' ~$27M wrongful liquidation event; Chaos Labs post-mortem 'Exchange Rate Misalignment on wstETH Core and Prime Instances' goes up on the Aave governance forum (thread 24269).
TokenLogic files '[Direct to AIP] wstETH CAPO Oracle Incident User Reimbursement' (thread 24275): total refund 512.19 ETH to the 34 affected accounts; net DAO cost 357.56 ETH after recoveries.

Early restitution: ~141.5 ETH of liquidator profits clawed back via BuilderNet refunds (plus ~13 ETH in liquidation fees) flows to affected users; DAO treasury commitment capped around 345-358 ETH covers the remainder.

Media tallies the incident as one of '4 setbacks in 12 days' for Aave; AAVE token trades down (~$125 to ~$108 area over the surrounding days — partially broader-market and other-news driven, not cleanly attributable).

Chaos Labs announces exit as Aave's risk manager (role held since Nov 2022), citing unprofitability, a V4-migration methodology/budget dispute with Aave Labs ($8M asked vs $5M offered) and legal-liability concerns to which the CAPO incident contributed; follows earlier exits of BGD Labs and Aave Chan Initiative; LlamaRisk absorbs risk coverage.

Reimbursement reported finalized for all 34 affected accounts (initial 141 ETH BuilderNet refund + DAO treasury top-up); August 2026 retrospectives treat the event as the canonical 'oracle staleness without an oracle hack' failure mode.

wstETH_aave_oracle_rate_eth_terms.window: 2026-03-10 intraday. NOT a USD market move: Aave's CAPO cap priced wstETH at ~1.1939 ETH vs live on-chain rate ~1.2285 ETH (some sources cite the stored snapshotRatio ~1.1919 vs cap ~1.1939 distinction). The wstETH/stETH secondary market and Lido exchange rate were unaffected.

wstETH_market_price.window: No genuine market move accompanied the liquidations — this is the defining feature of the event; the mispricing was purely internal to Aave's oracle cap.

AAVE_token.window: ~2026-03-10 to mid-March (invezz/TradingView). Caution: only ~-3% was attributed to the incident week itself; the $125->$108 slide overlaps broader market weakness and other Aave negative news — do not model as pure event impact.

liquidated_positions.window: 34 borrower accounts lost ~499-512 ETH in liquidation penalties on ~$26-27M of closed positions (2026-03-10); later reimbursed in full.

defi_impact.protocol: Aave V3 Ethereum — Core and Prime instances only (other chains/instances unaffected)
defi_impact.collateral_affected: wstETH (Lido wrapped staked ETH) used in ETH-correlated E-Mode; borrowed asset predominantly WETH/ETH
defi_impact.liquidated: ~10,938 wstETH across 34 accounts, ~$26-27M notional (The Block: $26M; CoinDesk et al.: $27M; one outlier $21.7M); ~499-512 ETH in liquidation bonuses captured by bots
defi_impact.suppliers_affected: NO — this is the key fact for a USDC-supplier book. Liquidity pools were untouched, no supplier haircut, no withdrawal freeze, zero bad debt (over-collateralized positions were liquidated 2.85% too early, which if anything over-protects suppliers). Losses fell exclusively on the 34 wrongfully liquidated BORROWERS via liquidation penalties, and were then socialized to the DAO treasury through reimbursement.
defi_impact.operational_response: wstETH borrow caps temporarily slashed on Core/Prime during the emergency, re-enabled by follow-up Direct-to-AIP (thread 24295); snapshot parameters manually realigned same day
defi_impact.governance_fallout: Accelerated Aave's 2026 service-provider exodus: Chaos Labs exited as risk manager 2026-04-06 (legal-liability concerns for risk providers cited), after BGD Labs and ACI departures; LlamaRisk took over risk coverage — leaving the largest DeFi lender briefly without its long-time dedicated risk manager

causes.root_cause: Parameter desynchronization inside Aave's CAPO (Correlated/Capped Asset Price Oracle) adapter for wstETH: an automated snapshotRatio update was clamped by the adapter's growth-rate constraint (moved only ~1.1572 -> ~1.1919 instead of the intended ~1.2282), while snapshotTimestamp updated unimpeded to an anchor ~7 days in the past. The cap formula (snapshotRatio grown forward at maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent since snapshotTimestamp) then produced a ceiling ~1.1939 wstETH/ETH, ~2.85% BELOW the live rate ~1.2285 — inverting CAPO's purpose (it exists to cap upside manipulation of LST exchange rates, and should never bind below the true rate).
causes.proximate_trigger: 2026-03-10 11:46 UTC: Chaos Labs' off-chain Edge Risk engine computed/submitted the flawed update; BGD Labs' AgentHub executed it on-chain one block later via Chainlink Automation, with no sanity cross-check against the live on-chain exchange rate before liquidations became eligible.
causes.amplifier: Permissionless liquidation bots acted within blocks on the 34 ETH-correlated E-Mode positions (high leverage, thin health-factor buffers), so a 2.85% oracle-only haircut was enough to push them 'underwater' on paper.
causes.what_it_was_NOT: Not a hack/exploit, not a Chainlink feed failure, not an Aave smart-contract bug, not a market crash — no underlying price moved. Chaos Labs and Stani Kulechov both characterized it as a misconfiguration of an external risk tool.
causes.responsibility: Chaos Labs (risk manager operating the CAPO parameters/Edge engine) owned the error; the Aave DAO accepted reimbursement responsibility; the incident fed Chaos Labs' April 6, 2026 exit as Aave risk manager.

contagion: None to markets: wstETH's actual exchange rate and secondary-market price never moved; no depeg, no cross-protocol liquidation cascade, no stablecoin involvement.
Contained to Aave V3 Ethereum Core and Prime instances; other Aave deployments and other lending protocols unaffected.

Governance/vendor contagion was the real transmission channel: the incident sharpened legal-liability fears for DeFi risk providers and fed Chaos Labs' 2026-04-06 exit as Aave risk manager, following BGD Labs and Aave Chan Initiative departures — briefly leaving ~$50B TVL without a dedicated risk manager (LlamaRisk stepped in).
Reputational clustering: media counted it among '4 setbacks in 12 days' for Aave in March 2026; AAVE token softness (~$125 -> ~$108) was partially coincident with broader market weakness.

Do not conflate with the SEPARATE April 2026 KelpDAO/rsETH exploit (~$292M stolen), which DID cause ~$200M bad debt on Aave and a ~$6B TVL drop — that later event, not CAPO, is the supplier-loss scenario; CAPO itself left suppliers whole.

recovery.technical: Same-day fix: Chaos Labs cut wstETH borrow caps and manually realigned snapshotRatio/snapshotTimestamp, restoring correct CAPO pricing on 2026-03-10; borrow caps re-enabled shortly after via Direct-to-AIP (thread 24295).
recovery.financial: Liquidations were not reversible on-chain; users were made whole in ETH instead. Recoveries: 141.5 ETH of liquidator profit clawed back via BuilderNet refunds plus ~13 ETH in liquidation fees, distributed to affected users as an early refund (~141 ETH). TokenLogic's Direct-to-AIP (filed 2026-03-11) set total restitution at 512.19 ETH with net DAO treasury cost of 357.56 ETH (early reports framed the treasury cap as ~345-358 ETH).
recovery.status_as_of_2026_08: Multiple outlets and an Aug 2026 retrospective report compensation finalized for all 34 affected accounts — full reimbursement. Exact on-chain payout execution date not independently verified from available sources.
recovery.structural: CAPO parameter-update process reviewed across Aave markets; incident became a reference case for adding live-rate sanity checks to automated risk-parameter pipelines. Longer-term: risk-provider turnover (Chaos Labs out, LlamaRisk in) as of April 2026.
recovery.duration_to_full_recovery: Oracle: same day. User balances: days (BuilderNet portion) to weeks (DAO treasury portion). Protocol solvency: never impaired (zero bad debt).

confidence_notes: Overall confidence: HIGH on event existence, date/time, mechanism, no-bad-debt/no-supplier-loss finding, and reimbursement structure — each is corroborated by 3+ independent outlets plus the governance-forum record. MEDIUM on exact figures where sources genuinely disagree: total liquidated is reported as $26M (The Block), ~$26.9M, and $27M (CoinDesk/Cointelegraph), with one $21.7M outlier — I report the $26-27M range; liquidation bonuses appear as both ~499 ETH and ~512 ETH (the 512.19 ETH AIP refund equals gross penalties, 499 ETH is likely net of the ~13 ETH fee component); the capped rate appears as both ~1.1919 (stored snapshotRatio) and ~1.1939 (extrapolated ceiling) — these are two different quantities in the same mechanism, both reported. The brief's $27.78M could NOT be confirmed in any live source and should be replaced with the $26-27M range. LOW confidence items, left qualified: exact correction minute, exact treasury-payout execution date, and the AAVE token move's attribution (confounded window). Method caveat: the sandbox egress proxy blocked all direct page fetches, so verification relied on cross-matching nine independent web-search result sets quoting the primary sources; no number here rests on a single outlet. For the SPA USDC book the load-bearing conclusion is robust: this was wrongful liquidation of BORROWERS only — zero bad debt, USDC suppliers completely unaffected — i.e., an operational near-miss for a supplier book, whose supplier-loss analogue is the separate April 2026 Kelp/rsETH event.

spa_relevance.book: $100k USDC: Aave v3 40% / Pendle PT 20% / Maple 15% / Morpho Steakhouse USDC 15% / cash 10%
spa_relevance.aave_v3_40pct: A USDC supplier on Aave V3 Ethereum would have experienced ZERO loss and zero disruption: no bad debt, pools untouched, withdrawals normal, and the event even nets positive to reserves (liquidation fees). The event materializes VENUE-OPERATIONAL risk, not credit risk: the same automation chain (off-chain risk engine -> on-chain executor, no live-rate sanity check) could in a mirrored failure OVER-value collateral or delay legitimate liquidations, which WOULD create bad debt hitting suppliers. Treat as evidence that 40% single-venue concentration carries correlated oracle-governance/ops risk that TVL and utilization metrics do not capture — and note the vendor-instability tail (risk manager exited 4 weeks later).
spa_relevance.pendle_pt_20pct: No impact on USDC-yield PTs. Advisory: Pendle PT collateral listed on Aave is priced via analogous capped/linear-discount oracles — the same misconfiguration class applies to PT markets; PT positions on ETH-correlated underlyings would have been in the blast radius.
spa_relevance.maple_15pct: No impact (institutional credit pools, no CAPO/wstETH exposure).
spa_relevance.morpho_steakhouse_15pct: No direct impact. Analogous risk: MetaMorpho vaults allocate to isolated markets whose oracles are curator-configured; a curator/oracle misconfiguration is the same failure family, and on Morpho losses from a mispriced market WOULD flow to vault suppliers (no DAO treasury backstop of Aave's size).
spa_relevance.stress_test_use: Model as a zero-NAV-loss operational near-miss with a defined tail variant: (a) base replay = 0% book impact, possible 1-day precautionary freeze of new Aave allocations (fail-closed posture per SPA RiskPolicy); (b) tail variant = sign-flipped or larger misconfig on a debt or collateral asset creating supplier-side bad debt (for calibration: the separate Apr 2026 Kelp/rsETH exploit DID hit Aave with ~$200M bad debt and a ~$6B TVL drop — that scenario, not this one, is the supplier-loss analogue). Also validates SPA's live-TVL/fail-closed invariants: the wrongful print was detectable by cross-checking the oracle cap vs the live on-chain exchange rate — exactly the class of feed-divergence refusal SPA's quorum logic is built for.

assumptions: Исторически честный тихий контроль: USDC-саплаер не терял ничего; ценность сценария — в датасете (класс «оракульная КОНФИГУРАЦИЯ», venue-операционный риск) и в вопросе к тирингу площадки, не в P&L.
